steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Conformity is changing your behaviour or beliefs to fit in with a group. Internalisation: genuinely accepting group norms (deep, lasting change). Identification: adopting group behaviour to gain membership. Compliance: going along publicly but not privately changing. | Key Fact: Asch's (1951) line conformity experiment: 75% of participants conformed at least once, giving a clearly wrong answer. Conformity increased with group size (up to 3) and unanimity, but decreased with a dissenting partner. | Key Fact: Milgram's (1963) obedience study: 65% of participants delivered the maximum 450V shock when instructed by an authority figure. Obedience increased with proximity of authority, legitimacy of the institution, and uniform. | Key Fact: Zimbardo's (1973) Stanford Prison Experiment:
